narrative:
Your loan application has been reviewed by our credit assessment system, which determined an 81% likelihood that you represent a high credit risk — a result that led to the denial of your application. This is a significant probability, and understanding the specific reasons behind this outcome can help you take meaningful steps toward a successful application in the future.

The most influential factor in this decision was the length of your requested loan term. You applied for a 60-month loan, which is more than three times the average duration of approximately 19 months seen among applicants who were approved. A longer repayment period increases the uncertainty around your ability to sustain payments over time, and this substantially pushed the assessment toward a higher risk rating.

The second major concern relates to your checking account status. Your account currently holds between 0 and 200 Deutsche Marks, which places you in a financially thin position. Among approved applicants, over half had no checking account at all or maintained healthier balances, and the model interpreted your low balance as a signal of limited financial cushion to handle loan repayments alongside everyday expenses.

The third factor that weighed against your application is your property situation. You indicated having no property or assets of unknown value, which means there is no tangible collateral backing your loan. In contrast, the majority of approved applicants owned real estate, a vehicle, or held life insurance — assets that provide security to lenders. Without such backing, the risk to the lender is considerably higher.

It is worth noting that some aspects of your profile are not unusual — your employment duration of one to four years and your credit history of existing paid credits are both common among approved applicants. However, the combination of a very long loan term, a large requested amount of 6,288 DM (compared to an average of around 2,887 DM among approved applicants), and the absence of meaningful assets created a profile that the system assessed as too risky to approve.

To improve your chances in a future application, you might consider requesting a shorter loan term and a smaller amount, building up savings or securing a guarantor, and if possible, establishing a stronger asset base before reapplying.
